children: By Mohi Narayan, Trixie Yap and Jeslyn Lerh

Oil product stocks held in Asia's key fuel trading hub Singapore rose to the highest level since May 27 due to a large increase in light distillate inventories, government data released on Thursday showed.
Combined onshore oil product inventories were at 42.64 million barrels in the week ended September 16, data from Enterprise Singapore showed, compared with 40.47 million barrels a week earlier.
LIGHT, MIDDLE DISTILLATES STOCKS GAIN
Light distillates stocks, including naphtha and gasoline, rose to 13.81 million barrels, also the highest level since May 27, the data showed.
Gasoline imports totalled about 303,000 metric tons (approximately 2.6 million barrels) during the period, while exports reached roughly 785,000 tons.

Outbound gasoline volumes were led by Indonesia at about 362,000 tons, followed by Australia at around 132,000 tons. Gasoline inflows were led by Taiwan at nearly 125,000 tons, followed by China at about 74,000 tons.
Naphtha imports stood at about 162,000 tons (approximately 1.5 million barrels), led by Kuwait at nearly 48,000 tons, followed by Trinidad and Tobago at around 31,000 tons.
Singapore exported about 13,900 tons of naphtha, with all shipments destined for Indonesia.
Middle distillates stocks climbed for a second straight week to hit nearly 8.7 million barrels, their highest in nearly a month.
Net exports for diesel and gasoil fell by 61% from a week ago, while imports swelled by nearly three times from a week ago.
Arrivals from China, South Korea and Malaysia were most prevalent, in line with earlier expectations, with traders expecting these volumes to continue flowing in the near term.
Exports of the transport and industrial fuel were little changed from a week ago, with export destinations mostly Indonesia and Malaysia.
On the jet fuel front, net exports rose 75% from a week earlier as total imports fell by 100% over the same period.
RESIDUAL FUEL STOCKS DECLINE
Residual fuel inventories remained above 20 million barrels, though edging slightly lower week on week.
Stockpiles dipped 1% at 20.14 million barrels (3.17 million tons), down for a second week, data showed.
Despite the slight declines, the inventories averaged higher this month versus last month's 18.6 million barrels.
Imports of fuel oil more than doubled to over 915,000 tons. Brazil was the top supplier of volumes for the week, followed by the United Arab Emirates.
Meanwhile, exports of fuel oil gained 44.6% week on week to above 223,000 tons, with most volumes headed for China and Taiwan.
Spot premiums of fuel oil showed shown some signs of easing this week, though retaining a floor as supply uncertainties lingered.
